request.spec:
Show on each person their settled-total (the due of their SETTLED claims that count, at
their frozen figures, corrections included) and their open-total (the due of their OPEN and
PENDING claims that count: a held, deferred or retired-and-excluded claim is left out as it is
from the due-total). Show the sheet's settled-total and open-total too, each simply everyone's
figure added up (not trimmed). The two must add up to the person's untrimmed due-total before the
cap.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Show on each person their settled-total (the due of their SETTLED claims that count, at
their frozen figures, corrections included) and their open-total (the due of their OPEN and
PENDING claims that count: a held, deferred or retired-and-excluded claim is left out as it is
from the due-total). Show the sheet's settled-total and open-total too, each simply everyone's
figure added up (not trimmed). The two must add up to the person's untrimmed due-total before the
cap.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Each person now shows a settled-total and an open-total, and the sheet shows both totals as well. I ran `bin/e2e` and all 4 tests in the spec pass.

The change is front-end only, because the app already works out its due figures in the browser. No stored data, server code or audit records needed to change.

- **The calculation:** I added `settledAndOpen` to `src/main/frontend/features/rates/ratesQuery.ts`. It takes the person's claims that count, using the same rule the due-total uses. That rule already leaves out held, deferred and retired-and-excluded open claims, and drafts and voided claims. It then splits them two ways:
  - **Settled-total:** the person's SETTLED claims at their frozen figures, corrections included.
  - **Open-total:** the person's OPEN and PENDING claims at their current figures.

  Neither is capped, so the two always add up to the person's due-total before the cap.
- **On screen** (`src/main/frontend/features/rates/due.slot.tsx`):
  - Each person row has two new columns, Settled and Open, placed after Due (`person-settled-total`, `person-open-total`).
  - A new line in the sheet panel, below the due-total, shows `rollup-settled-total` and `rollup-open-total`. Each is everyone's figure added up, with no highest or lowest left out.

The sheet totals include every person on the sheet, retired people too.
